meta.title: Competitor Radar
meta.niche: Fast, AI-assisted email client software for professionals and teams

analysis.summary: Mailbird is the only direct rival publishing at volume, with 40 new pages in 30 days. Superhuman, Spark, Shortwave and Missive are nearly silent.

points.text: Mailbird published 40 new pages, mostly comparisons and how-tos, and names Spark, Outlook and Apple Mail as targets. Superhuman wasn't named in any title.
Front published 17 new pages and updated 9 older ones, but it targets customer support teams. It is not a direct email-client rival.
Superhuman, Spark, Shortwave and Missive published almost nothing new. Spark's only two pages are one launch post and its translation.

Superhuman.play: One new how-to on the inbox zero method. Otherwise quiet, with 136 templated store pages.

Shortwave.play: No new or updated pages in 30 days. No visible content push.

Spark Mail.play: Launched Auto-Drafts (AI-written replies) with one English post and one Ukrainian translation.

Front.play: Mass-produces comparison and how-to guides, and refreshes product pages around AI agents for support.
Front.aimed: B2B customer support and operations teams

Missive.play: No new or updated pages. Its 338 changelog pages are templated and not counted.

Mailbird.play: Floods search with comparisons, 'best of 2026' lists and how-tos, with many Spark and Outlook alternatives.
Mailbird.aimed: Windows and Mac users comparing email clients

shared.title: Comparison pages
shared.text: Mailbird (19) and Front (8) publish many 'alternatives' and 'best of' pages to catch people choosing a tool. Superhuman has none, so rivals own those searches.

shared.title: Email how-to guides
shared.text: Mailbird (18) and Front (7) publish explainers on practical problems. Superhuman has one how-to, so it is thin in this area.

gaps.title: Premium AI email comparisons
gaps.text: Mailbird's 'Best AI Email Client' page is the only one in this set. Superhuman could own 'fast, premium, AI email' comparisons on its own terms.

gaps.title: Role-based email workflows
gaps.text: Only Mailbird covers lawyers, teachers, students and photographers. Superhuman could publish guides for founders, sales, recruiters and execs, who fit its premium buyers.

gaps.title: Team email and shared inbox guides
gaps.text: Nobody here, apart from Front's support-focused pages, covers fast team email for professionals. Superhuman could own team workflow content.

versus.Shortwave: Shortwave published nothing in 30 days, as did Superhuman's one new page by comparison, so neither is pushing content.
versus.Spark Mail: Spark posted only an Auto-Drafts launch and its translation, while Superhuman posted one how-to. Both are quiet, but Spark is the main target of Mailbird's comparisons.
versus.Front: Front publishes far more and aims at support teams, while Superhuman's content is almost absent and aimed at individual email habits.
versus.Missive: Missive published no new pages, like Superhuman's near-silence, and relies on a large templated changelog.
versus.Mailbird: Mailbird publishes 40 pages of comparisons and how-tos against Superhuman's one, and it competes for searches Superhuman does not contest.
